sonnet.problem: The blank asks the baker to complete the wording of a line ('justice and ___'). No earlier card has shown that wording, so the baker cannot reason it out. The right answer is also the only Bible-sounding word. 'Fear' and 'conquest' are filler.
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: The joke compares David dedicating gold and silver to the LORD with Papa Dorin putting something shiny on the counter for everybody to see. The actions don't match: David dedicates the gifts to the LORD, while Dorin shows off. It also makes a holy act sound like display, and it repeats the earlier 'shiny gold' joke about the gold base.
sonnet.rule: The everyday comparison must have the same action.
